intro: I speak at conferences, schools, universities, companies and parliamentary events about how young people grow up well: their mental health, their education and the route from school into work.

topics.title: Mental health: prevention and early intervention
topics.for: Conferences, charities, health and education leaders
topics.summary: Why support needs to arrive before crisis point, what early help looks like from a young person's side, and what years of campaigning for it taught me.

topics.title: What young people need from education
topics.summary: Pressure, exams and how we measure success, and what schools could look like if they were built around the young people in them, in a world that keeps changing.

topics.title: Schools and sixth forms: finding what drives you
topics.summary: An honest talk for students about trying different things, getting it wrong, looking after yourself and working out what you care about.

topics.title: From school to work: pre-careers and early careers
topics.for: Employers, early careers teams, careers leaders
topics.summary: How the route into work is changing, what young people are not being told, and what employers can do to make the first rung reachable.

topics.title: For graduates and universities
topics.summary: Building experience alongside a degree, and creating your own ladder when the usual graduate pathways are narrowing.

topics.title: Mental health policy and education policy
topics.for: Policy events, think tanks, parliamentary audiences
topics.summary: An evidence-led view from a young person who has spent years listening to other young people, on where policy is working and where it is missing them.

topics.title: How organisations can engage young people properly
topics.summary: Moving past the one-off youth panel: what meaningful youth voice looks like, and how to build it into decisions. Nothing about us, without us.

faq.q: What does Stefano Di Rico speak about?
faq.a: Young people's mental health, prevention and early intervention; education and what young people need from it; pre-career development and the route from school to work, including early careers and graduates; mental health policy and education policy; and how organisations can engage young people properly.

faq.q: What kinds of events does he speak at?
faq.a: Conferences, schools and sixth forms, universities, companies and parliamentary events. He gives keynotes, joins and chairs panels, runs workshops, and records live episodes of his podcast, Creating Your Ladder.
Venues and events include the London Assembly, the British Library, the Children's Media Conference and the Italian Cultural Institute in London.

faq.q: How do I book Stefano to speak?
faq.a: Email hello@di-rico.com with the date, the audience and what you would like him to cover. Get in touch about availability and fees.
Yes. He speaks in schools, sixth forms and universities about mental health, finding what motivates you and the route into work.

faq.q: Is there a bio and photo I can use to introduce him?
faq.a: Yes. The press kit has bios at 50, 100 and 250 words, headshots to download and a suggested introduction for event hosts.
